english.question:
Exert

1. The athlete had to exert all his strength to lift the heavy weights during the competition.

2. The government plans to exert a new policy to improve economic growth in rural areas.

3. She continued to exert a positive influence on her students even after retirement.
english.common_data: In each of the following questions, a highlighted word is given and used in the three statements. You have to identify in which of the following statements the word is correctly used, and mark it as your answer. If all sentences are correct, choose option E as your answer.
english.explanation:
Answer: D

Sentence 1: The word “exert” is correctly used to mean applying physical effort or strength, which is the standard usage of the word.

Sentence 2: The word “exert” is incorrect. One does not “exert” a policy; policies are implemented, introduced, or enforced. A word like “implement” or “introduce” would be appropriate here.

Sentence 3: The word “exert” is correctly used to indicate applying or bringing to bear a positive influence, which fits the proper meaning of the word.

So, Sentences 1 and 3 use exert in a grammatically correct and contextually meaningful manner.

Therefore, option d) Both 1 and 3 is the correct choice.

english.question:
Proscribe

1. The doctor decided to proscribe antibiotics to treat the patient’s severe infection.

2. She proscribed a detailed plan for the upcoming project to ensure its success.

3. The government decided to proscribe the use of certain harmful chemicals in consumer products.
english.common_data: In each of the following questions, a highlighted word is given and used in the three statements. You have to identify in which of the following statements the word is correctly used, and mark it as your answer. If all sentences are correct, choose option E as your answer.
english.explanation:
Answer: C

Sentence 1: The word “proscribe” is incorrect. It means to forbid or prohibit, whereas the sentence intends to convey recommending or ordering medication. The correct word here is “prescribe.”

Sentence 2: The word “proscribe” is incorrect. It does not mean to recommend or outline a plan; it refers to banning or condemning something. A word like “prescribed” or “outlined” would be appropriate.

Sentence 3: The word “proscribe” is correctly used to mean officially forbidding or prohibiting the use of harmful chemicals, aligning with the word’s standard definition.

So, Sentence 3 uses proscribe in a grammatically correct and contextually meaningful manner.

Therefore, option c) Only 3 is the correct choice.

english.question: The team leader, who everyone thought were the strongest candidate, was surprisingly dropped from the final selection list.
english.common_data: A part of the sentence is highlighted. Four alternatives marked as (A), (B), (C) and (D) are given as substitutions for the highlighted part, one of which will improve the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed, choose the option “No improvement required” i.e. (E).
english.explanation:
Answer: A

The structure here is: who [everyone thought] was...
"Everyone thought" is an embedded reporting clause - it does not change the fact that "who" refers to "the team leader" - singular.
So the verb must be singular: "was", not "were".
Also, since "thought" is past, the embedded clause uses past tense "was" (backshift: is - was).
"were the strongest candidate" - plural verb; "who" refers to singular "team leader"
B) "is the strongest candidate" - present tense; fails backshift after "thought"
C) "had been the strongest candidates" - plural "candidates"; singular subject; wrong
D) "would be the strongest candidate" - conditional; wrong structure here
A) "was the strongest candidate" - singular + past backshift; correct

The team leader, who everyone thought was the strongest candidate, was surprisingly dropped.

english.question: He prevented his younger brother to make the same mistake that had cost him so dearly in his early career.
english.common_data: A part of the sentence is highlighted. Four alternatives marked as (A), (B), (C) and (D) are given as substitutions for the highlighted part, one of which will improve the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed, choose the option “No improvement required” i.e. (E).
english.explanation:
Answer: D

The verb "prevent" always follows the pattern:
prevent + object + from + gerund (-ing)

It never takes a to-infinitive after the object.
"prevented him to make" - to-infinitive; wrong pattern after prevent

A) "from to make" - "from + infinitive" is wrong; needs gerund
B) "to making" - "to + gerund" is not standard
C) "against making" - "against" is not used after prevent
D) "from making" - prevent + from + gerund; the only correct pattern
Similar patterns: stop someone from doing / refrain from doing / keep someone from doing

Correct: He prevented his younger brother from making the same mistake...

english.question: The Finance Minister stated that the government would ________ additional funds to the health sector in the revised budget estimates to strengthen primary care infrastructure.
english.common_data: In the following questions, a sentence is given with a blank in it. It is then followed by five alternatives among which, one of the words fits correctly in the given blank so as to make the sentence meaningful. Find out the most suitable word and mark it as your answer.
english.explanation:
Answer: C

a) divert - Incorrect. "Divert funds" means to redirect money away from its original purpose, often with a negative connotation. The sentence describes a positive budgetary move toward health, not a redirection away from something else.

b) freeze - Incorrect. "Freeze funds" means to stop access to or movement of money. This is the opposite of what is described - the government is channelling more money, not stopping it.

c) allocate - Correct. "Allocate funds" is the standard official and budgetary term meaning to set aside a specific amount of money for a particular purpose. It fits precisely with "revised budget estimates."

d) borrow - Incorrect. "Borrow funds" means to take money on credit. While governments do borrow, the sentence is about directing funds to health infrastructure, not about the source of those funds.

e) retain - Incorrect. "Retain funds" means to keep money in reserve or hold it back. This implies the funds stay where they are, whereas the sentence clearly indicates a fresh infusion into the health sector.

english.question: The CEO reminded the employees that the annual bonus depends on the company's overall performance and individual KPIs for the year.
english.common_data: A part of the sentence is highlighted. Four alternatives marked as (A), (B), (C) and (D) are given as substitutions for the highlighted part, one of which will improve the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed, choose the option “No improvement required” i.e. (E).
english.explanation:
Answer: E

Normally, reported speech requires backshift after a past reporting verb ("reminded"). But there is a key exception:
Exception: When the subordinate clause expresses a general truth, standing policy, or current fact, the present tense is retained.
"The annual bonus depends on performance" is a standing company policy - it is true now and in the future, not just at the time of speaking. So the present tense "depends" is correctly retained.

A) "depended" - past tense; implies the policy no longer applies
B) "would depend" - conditional; weakens the policy statement unnecessarily
C) "had depended" - past perfect; implies the policy ended before the meeting
D) "will depend" - future; present simple is more natural for a standing policy
E) No improvement - "depends" correctly expresses the standing company policy

Correct: The CEO reminded the employees that the annual bonus depends on the company's overall performance…

english.question: Which of the following is the penultimate sentence after rearrangement?
english.common_data:
In the given question, sentences are given in jumbled form. Rearrange them in proper order and answer the questions that follow.

Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph:

A. For the first time in the history of the National Defence Academy, a batch of women cadets successfully completed their training and were commissioned as officers of the Indian Army.

B. The Indian Military Academy in Dehradun is one of India's most prestigious institutions for training officers of the Indian Army, and it recently witnessed a historic moment during its Passing Out Parade.

C. President Droupadi Murmu, who serves as the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, reviewed the parade and formally recognised the achievement of these pioneering women officers.

D. The commissioning of India's first NDA female batch marks a proud turning point in the country's military history and sends a strong message about equal opportunity and the changing face of national service.

E. This landmark event is seen as a significant step towards greater gender inclusion within the Indian armed forces, a journey that began when the Supreme Court opened the doors of the NDA to women in the year 2021.
english.explanation:
The paragraph discusses the historic commissioning of the first batch of women officers trained through the National Defence Academy (NDA), highlighting its significance for gender inclusion in the Indian armed forces.

The paragraph begins with sentence B, which introduces the setting-the Indian Military Academy-and mentions a historic moment during its Passing Out Parade. Sentence A follows by explaining what that historic moment was: the commissioning of the first batch of women NDA cadets as Army officers. Sentence C adds an important event associated with the ceremony, namely President Droupadi Murmu reviewing the parade and recognising the achievement. Sentence E then explains the broader significance of this milestone by linking it to the Supreme Court's 2021 decision allowing women to enter the NDA. Finally, sentence D concludes the passage by summarising the historic importance of the event and its message of equal opportunity.

So, the correct sequence is: B - A - C - E - D.

Answer: D

The penultimate sentence in a paragraph is the one that appears just before the last sentence and serves as a bridge or transition to the final point. In this sequence, Sentence E, “This landmark event is seen as a significant step towards greater gender inclusion within the Indian armed forces, a journey that began when the Supreme Court opened the doors of the NDA to women in the year 2021.” is the penultimate sentence.

b) manageable - Correct. "Manageable" means within controllable limits and not a cause for concern. It is the most fitting word given that the sentence attributes stability to positive economic factors - a typical economic commentary phrasing.

The phrase "along with his two colleagues" is additional information and does not affect the subject-verb agreement.

The correct structure is: Singular subject + along with + additional phrase + singular verb.

Hence, the corrected sentence is: "Mr. Sharma, along with his two colleagues, was awarded the prestigious national research grant for their groundbreaking work."

Other options are incorrect:

A) Incorrect: "were being awarded" changes the meaning to an ongoing action and does not match the sentence structure.

B) Incorrect: “have been awarded” Changes the tense from simple past to present perfect.

D) Incorrect: "had being awarded" is grammatically incorrect; the correct form would be had been awarded.

E) Incorrect: The original sentence has a subject–verb agreement error (were → was).

english.question: What was India's GDP growth rate in the January–March 2026 quarter, and how did it compare to market expectations?
english.common_data:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:

India’s economy delivered a stellar performance in the January-March quarter of 2026. GDP growth came in at 7.8 per cent, easing slightly from 8 per cent in the preceding quarter but comfortably above market expectations of 7.2 per cent, taking full-year FY26 growth to 7.7 per cent. Prime Minister Modi has every reason to proclaim India the world’s fastest-growing major economy. The number is real. The achievement is genuine. But a number, however impressive, is not the full story. Look past the headline, and the stress fractures become visible. Begin with the central bank.

The Reserve Bank of India held its repo rate steady at 5.25 per cent for the third consecutive meeting in June, maintaining a neutral stance even as it cut its GDP growth forecast for FY2026-27 sharply to 6.6 per cent from an earlier 6.9 per cent. A central bank that simultaneously freezes rates and slashes its own growth projection is not a central bank radiating confidence. It is one navigating a tightrope. Inflation is now projected to average 5.1 per cent for the current fiscal year, up significantly from an earlier estimate of 4.6 per cent. The “rare Goldilocks” era that RBI Governor Malhotra celebrated just months ago has quietly given way to stagflationary risk. Then there is the rupee downslide.

Foreign investors have offloaded over $20 billion in Indian shares so far this year, placing the rupee under severe pressure and making it one of Asia’s worst-performing major currencies in 2026. A sliding currency is more than a financial statistic - it is a barometer of confidence, and right now that barometer is falling.  Capital outflows of $13.7 billion from the equity segment alone since January have prompted the RBI to roll out emergency measures to attract foreign capital.

The global backdrop adds further complexity. Economists have cautioned that growth is likely to moderate this year amid rising energy costs and global uncertainty linked to the West Asia conflict. India’s ability to source affordable energy has been disrupted, and the RBI’s own revised growth trajectory for FY27 ranges between 6.3 per cent and 6.8 per cent across quarters - a step down from FY26’s pace. What should India do to keep the momentum alive? Three imperatives stand out. First, protect the rupee without choking growth.

The RBI must strike a balance between currency stability and keeping borrowing costs conducive to investment. Deepening forex reserves, encouraging long-term capital inflows and reducing oil import dependence are the sustainable answers. Second, broaden the base of growth. While services, manufacturing and construction have driven the recent surge, agriculture grew just 3.6 per cent - a sector that still employs nearly half the workforce. Inclusive growth demands that rural incomes rise, farm productivity improves and the benefits of the services boom reach beyond Tier-1 cities. Third, stay fiscally disciplined. The temptation to spend India’s way through global headwinds is understandable, but deficit overruns would further spook foreign investors and weaken the rupee. The economy needs not just celebration, but honest diagnosis. The numbers are strong. The foundations need tending.
options: 8 per cent, which was exactly in line with market expectations.
7.2 per cent, which fell below market expectations of 7.8 per cent.
7.7 per cent, which was slightly below the market expectation of 8 per cent.
7.8 per cent, which was comfortably above the market expectation of 7.2 per cent.
6.9 per cent, which was well below the market expectation of 7.8 per cent.
english.explanation:
Answer: D

a) Incorrect. 8 per cent was the growth rate of the preceding quarter (October–December 2025), not January–March 2026. Market expectations were 7.2 per cent, not 8 per cent.

b) Incorrect. This reverses the numbers. 7.2 per cent was the market expectation, not the actual growth figure. Actual growth of 7.8 per cent beat, not missed, expectations.

c) Incorrect. 7.7 per cent is the full-year FY26 growth figure, not the January–March quarterly figure. The passage clearly distinguishes between the two.

d) Correct. The passage states: 'GDP growth came in at 7.8 per cent…comfortably above market expectations of 7.2 per cent' - directly matching this option.

e) Incorrect. 6.9 per cent is the RBI's earlier GDP forecast for FY2026-27, which was later revised downward. It has nothing to do with the January–March 2026 quarterly figure.

english.question: The Supreme Court observed that the state government had failed to ____ with the earlier order directing immediate relief to flood-affected families in the region.
english.common_data: In the following questions, a sentence is given with a blank in it. It is then followed by five alternatives among which, one of the words fits correctly in the given blank so as to make the sentence meaningful. Find out the most suitable word and mark it as your answer.
english.explanation:
Answer: B

a) interfere - Incorrect. "Interfere with an order" means to obstruct or meddle with it, not to follow it. The sentence is about the government's failure to act on the court's directions, not about obstructing them.

b) comply - Correct. "Comply with an order" is the precise legal and judicial phrase meaning to act in accordance with a directive. The Supreme Court's language in such contexts almost always uses "comply with."

c) negotiate - Incorrect. "Negotiate with an order" is not a standard collocation. Court orders are not negotiated - they are either followed or challenged. This option misunderstands the judicial process.

d) proceed - Incorrect. "Proceed with an order" might seem plausible but is not the standard term in legal usage. Moreover, it does not capture the obligation to carry out what was directed.

e) engage - Incorrect. "Engage with an order" is informal and vague. In legal context, engagement does not mean implementation. The sentence needs a word that signals full execution of the court's directive.

hindi.question: What was India's GDP growth rate in the January–March 2026 quarter, and how did it compare to market expectations?

India’s economy delivered a stellar performance in the January-March quarter of 2026. GDP growth came in at 7.8 per cent, easing slightly from 8 per cent in the preceding quarter but comfortably above market expectations of 7.2 per cent, taking full-year FY26 growth to 7.7 per cent. Prime Minister Modi has every reason to proclaim India the world’s fastest-growing major economy. The number is real. The achievement is genuine. But a number, however impressive, is not the full story. Look past the headline, and the stress fractures become visible. Begin with the central bank.

The Reserve Bank of India held its repo rate steady at 5.25 per cent for the third consecutive meeting in June, maintaining a neutral stance even as it cut its GDP growth forecast for FY2026-27 sharply to 6.6 per cent from an earlier 6.9 per cent. A central bank that simultaneously freezes rates and slashes its own growth projection is not a central bank radiating confidence. It is one navigating a tightrope. Inflation is now projected to average 5.1 per cent for the current fiscal year, up significantly from an earlier estimate of 4.6 per cent. The “rare Goldilocks” era that RBI Governor Malhotra celebrated just months ago has quietly given way to stagflationary risk. Then there is the rupee downslide.

Foreign investors have offloaded over $20 billion in Indian shares so far this year, placing the rupee under severe pressure and making it one of Asia’s worst-performing major currencies in 2026. A sliding currency is more than a financial statistic - it is a barometer of confidence, and right now that barometer is falling.  Capital outflows of $13.7 billion from the equity segment alone since January have prompted the RBI to roll out emergency measures to attract foreign capital.

A sliding currency is more than a financial statistic - it is a barometer of confidence, and right now that barometer is falling.  Capital outflows of $13.7 billion from the equity segment alone since January have prompted the RBI to roll out emergency measures to attract foreign capital.

The global backdrop adds further complexity. Economists have cautioned that growth is likely to moderate this year amid rising energy costs and global uncertainty linked to the West Asia conflict. India’s ability to source affordable energy has been disrupted, and the RBI’s own revised growth trajectory for FY27 ranges between 6.3 per cent and 6.8 per cent across quarters - a step down from FY26’s pace. What should India do to keep the momentum alive? Three imperatives stand out. First, protect the rupee without choking growth.

The RBI must strike a balance between currency stability and keeping borrowing costs conducive to investment. Deepening forex reserves, encouraging long-term capital inflows and reducing oil import dependence are the sustainable answers. Second, broaden the base of growth. While services, manufacturing and construction have driven the recent surge, agriculture grew just 3.6 per cent - a sector that still employs nearly half the workforce. Inclusive growth demands that rural incomes rise, farm productivity improves and the benefits of the services boom reach beyond Tier-1 cities. Third, stay fiscally disciplined. The temptation to spend India’s way through global headwinds is understandable, but deficit overruns would further spook foreign investors and weaken the rupee. The economy needs not just celebration, but honest diagnosis. The numbers are strong. The foundations need tending.
options: India's GDP growth of 7.8% proves it is the strongest economy in the world with no underlying risks.
The RBI's decision to hold the repo rate is damaging India's economic growth prospects.
India's strong GDP performance is real but masks serious underlying concerns including rupee pressure, inflation risk, and uneven growth that require honest policy attention.
Foreign investors are permanently leaving India's markets due to political instability.
Agriculture is the most important sector India must focus on to sustain its economic growth.
hindi.explanation:
Answer: C

a) Incorrect. The passage explicitly says 'a number, however impressive, is not the full story' and goes on to list stress fractures - ruling out any claim that there are no underlying risks.

b) Incorrect. The RBI's rate decision is one concern discussed, but the passage does not frame it as the cause of growth damage. The passage calls for balancing rate decisions, not criticising them outright.

c) Correct. The passage opens by acknowledging the genuine GDP achievement and then systematically unpacks the hidden stresses - RBI's downgraded forecasts, inflation risk, rupee slide, foreign outflows, and uneven sectoral growth - before offering three policy imperatives. This dual acknowledgement of strength and fragility is the central theme.

d) Incorrect. Foreign investors are selling Indian shares due to market pressures, but the passage presents this as a current challenge, not a permanent or politically driven exit.

e) Incorrect. Agriculture's slow growth is cited as one concern within the 'broaden the base' imperative, but it is a supporting detail - not the central theme of the passage.

hindi.question: The Supreme Court observed that the state government had failed to ____ with the earlier order directing immediate relief to flood-affected families in the region.
hindi.common_data: In the following questions, a sentence is given with a blank in it. It is then followed by five alternatives among which, one of the words fits correctly in the given blank so as to make the sentence meaningful. Find out the most suitable word and mark it as your answer.
hindi.explanation:
Answer: B

a) interfere - Incorrect. "Interfere with an order" means to obstruct or meddle with it, not to follow it. The sentence is about the government's failure to act on the court's directions, not about obstructing them.

b) comply - Correct. "Comply with an order" is the precise legal and judicial phrase meaning to act in accordance with a directive. The Supreme Court's language in such contexts almost always uses "comply with."

c) negotiate - Incorrect. "Negotiate with an order" is not a standard collocation. Court orders are not negotiated - they are either followed or challenged. This option misunderstands the judicial process.

d) proceed - Incorrect. "Proceed with an order" might seem plausible but is not the standard term in legal usage. Moreover, it does not capture the obligation to carry out what was directed.

e) engage - Incorrect. "Engage with an order" is informal and vague. In legal context, engagement does not mean implementation. The sentence needs a word that signals full execution of the court's directive.

hindi.question: A wild goose chase
hindi.common_data: In each of the following questions, an idiom is given. Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom.
options: A foolish and hopeless search for something unattainable.
A well-organized collective effort to solve a crisis.
hindi.explanation:
Answer: B

(a) Hunting expedition: Incorrect. This is a literalist fallacy, treating the metaphorical pursuit of an animal as an actual event.

(b) Foolish/hopeless search (Correct): Correct. It describes a pursuit or task that is entirely futile because the objective either does not exist or cannot be achieved.

(c) Strategic planning: Incorrect. This is a semantic contradiction, as the idiom implies a complete lack of structure and viability.

(d) Athletic competition: Incorrect. This is a contextual misattribution, confusing physical exertion with futility.

(e) Collective effort: Incorrect. This represents the antonym of the idiom's chaotic and unsuccessful connotation.

hindi.question: To face the music
hindi.common_data: In each of the following questions, an idiom is given. Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom.
options: To attend a concert or musical performance.
To express an artistic or creative opinion openly.
To accept the unpleasant consequences of one's actions.
To dismiss a serious problem with a cheerful attitude.
To undergo formal training in communication skills.
hindi.explanation:
Answer: C

(a) Attend a concert: Incorrect. This is a denotative error that interprets "music" literally rather than symbolically.

(b) Express artistic opinion: Incorrect. This is a domain error, restricting the phrase to the creative arts.

(c) Accept unpleasant consequences (Correct): Correct. It signifies confronting criticism, punishment, or retribution for a past mistake or failure.

(d) Dismiss a problem: Incorrect. This describes a state of denial or forced optimism, which is the opposite of facing accountability.

(e) Formal training: Incorrect. This is an irrelevant distractor with no semantic connection to the idiom.

english.question: A 144-litre mixture A contains milk and water, and the quantity of milk is 40% more than that of water. When 2x litres of mixture A are taken out, the quantity of water in mixture A becomes (x + 5) litres. If mixture B contains 5x litres and (2x – 10) litres of milk and water, then find the total quantity of mixture B.
english.explanation:
Answer: C

Let the initial quantity of water in mixture A be 5b litres.

So, the initial quantity of milk in mixture A= 1.4 * 5b = 7b litres

5b + 7b = 144

12b = 144

b = 12

The initial quantity of water in mixture A = 5 * 12 = 60 litres

The initial quantity of milk in mixture A = 7 * 12 = 84 litres

60 – {2x * (5/12)} = x+ 5

x + (5x/6) = 60 - 5

(11x/6) = 55

x = 30

The quantity of milk in mixtureB = 5 * 30 = 150 litres

The quantity of water in mixture B = 2 * 30 – 10 = 50 litres

The total quantity of milk and water in mixture B = (150 + 50) = 200 litres

Hence, the correct option is C.

english.question: The sum of the present ages of P, Q and R is 84 years. Six years ago, the age of P was three times the age of R, and at that same time, Q was 4 years younger than P. Find the present age of Q.

Answer: D

The present age of Q = 3x - 4 + 6 = 3x + 2

The present age of Q = 3x + 2 = 30 + 2 = 32 years 

Hence, the correct answer is option D.

english.question: Pipes A and B together can fill a tank in 80 hours, whereas pipes B and C together can fill the tank in 60 hours. english.explanation:
Answer: D

Let the total work = 240 units (LCM of 60 and 80)

The efficiency of pipe A and B = 240/80 = 3 units

The efficiency of pipe B and C = 240/60 = 4 units

The time taken by pipes A and B together to fill in 20 hours = 20 * 3 = 60 units

The time taken by pipes B and C together to fill in 15 hours = 15 * 4 = 60 units

The time taken by C alone to fill the tank in the remaining 60 hours = 240 - 60 - 60 = 120 units

The time taken by C alone to fill in one hour = 120/60 = 2 units

Time taken = 240/2 = 120 hours

english.question: A bag contains 90 color pencils of 3 types i.e. white, yellow and green. The number of yellow and green pencils are ‘x’ and ‘y’ respectively and the number of white pencils is 42. english.explanation:
Answer: D

Probability of drawing a yellow pencil from the bag = (x/90)

Probability of drawing a green pencil from the bag = (y/90)

Probability of drawing a yellow pencil = (4/15) + probability of drawing a green pencil

(x/90) = (4/15) + (y/90)

(x/90) – (y/90) = 4/15

(x-y)/90 = 4/15

x-y = 24 …eqn (1)

Total number of pencils in the bag = 90 and white pencils = 42

So, x + y + 42 = 90

x + y = 48 … eqn (2)

After equating eqn (1) and (2) we get, x= 36, y= 12

Therefore, the probability of drawing a green pencil = [(12C1)/ (90C1)] = 2/15

Hence, the correct option is D.

hindi.question: एकसाथ लेनोवो और एसुस द्वारा बेचे गए टैबलेट की कुल संख्या से एकसाथ डेल और एचपी द्वारा बेचे गए लैपटॉप की कुल संख्या का अनुपात ज्ञात कीजिए।
hindi.common_data:
निम्नलिखित जानकारी का ध्यानपूर्वक अध्ययन करें और नीचे दिए गए प्रश्नों के उत्तर दें।

दिया गया लाइन ग्राफ पांच कंपनियों अर्थात् - डेल, एचपी, लेनोवो, एसुस और एसर द्वारा बेचे गए टैबलेट और लैपटॉप की औसत संख्या के साथ-साथ प्रत्येक कंपनी द्वारा बेचे गए लैपटॉप की संख्या को दर्शाता है।

नोट: बेचे गए इलेक्ट्रॉनिक वस्तुओं की कुल संख्या = बेचे गए टैबलेट की संख्या + बेचे गए लैपटॉप की संख्या।
hindi.explanation:
डेल:

डेल द्वारा बेची गई इलेक्ट्रॉनिक वस्तुओं की कुल संख्या = 30 * 2 = 60

डेल द्वारा बेचे गए लैपटॉप की संख्या = 45

डेल द्वारा बेचे गए टैबलेट की संख्या = 60 - 45 = 15

एचपी:

एचपी द्वारा बेची गई इलेक्ट्रॉनिक वस्तुओं की कुल संख्या = 25 * 2 = 50

एचपी द्वारा बेचे गए लैपटॉप की संख्या = 40

एचपी द्वारा बेचे गए टैबलेट की संख्या = 50 - 40 = 10

लेनोवो:

लेनोवो द्वारा बेची गई इलेक्ट्रॉनिक वस्तुओं की कुल संख्या = 40 * 2 = 80

लेनोवो द्वारा बेचे गए लैपटॉप की संख्या = 60

लेनोवो द्वारा बेचे गए टैबलेट की संख्या = 80 - 60 = 20

एसुस:

एसुस द्वारा बेची गई इलेक्ट्रॉनिक वस्तुओं की कुल संख्या = 20 * 2 = 40

एसुस द्वारा बेचे गए लैपटॉप की संख्या = 25

एसुस द्वारा बेचे गए टैबलेट की संख्या = 40 - 25 = 15

एसर:

एसर द्वारा बेची गई इलेक्ट्रॉनिक वस्तुओं की कुल संख्या = 35 * 2 = 70

एसर द्वारा बेचे गए लैपटॉप की संख्या = 30

एसर द्वारा बेचे गए टैबलेट की संख्या = 70 - 30 = 40

उत्तर: D

एकसाथ लेनोवो और एसुस द्वारा बेचे गए टैबलेट की कुल संख्या = 20 + 15 = 35

एकसाथ डेल और एचपी द्वारा बेचे गए लैपटॉप की कुल संख्या = 45 + 40 = 85

आवश्यक अनुपात = 35 : 85 = 7 : 17

अतः, सही उत्तर विकल्प D है।

नीचे दी गई तालिका पांच अलग-अलग दुकानों अर्थात् - A, B, C, D और E द्वारा निर्मित वस्तुओं (मग और प्लेट) की कुल संख्या के साथ-साथ प्रत्येक दुकान द्वारा निर्मित मगों की संख्या से प्लेटों की संख्या के अनुपात को दर्शाती है।

नोट: निर्मित वस्तुओं की कुल संख्या = निर्मित मगों की संख्या + निर्मित प्लेटों की संख्या
hindi.explanation:
दुकान A:

दुकान A द्वारा निर्मित वस्तुओं की कुल संख्या = 720

दुकान A द्वारा निर्मित मगों की संख्या = 720 * (5/9) = 400

दुकान A द्वारा निर्मित प्लेटों की संख्या = 720 - 400 = 320

दुकान B:

दुकान B द्वारा निर्मित वस्तुओं की कुल संख्या = 600

दुकान B द्वारा निर्मित मगों की संख्या = 600 * (7/12) = 350

दुकान B द्वारा निर्मित प्लेटों की संख्या = 600 - 350 = 250

दुकान C:

दुकान C द्वारा निर्मित वस्तुओं की कुल संख्या = 840

दुकान C द्वारा निर्मित मगों की संख्या = 840 * (4/7) = 480

दुकान C द्वारा निर्मित प्लेटों की संख्या = 840 - 480 = 360

दुकान D:

दुकान D द्वारा निर्मित वस्तुओं की कुल संख्या = 540

दुकान D द्वारा निर्मित मगों की संख्या = 540 * (2/3) = 360

दुकान D द्वारा निर्मित प्लेटों की संख्या = 540 - 360 = 180

दुकान E:

दुकान E द्वारा निर्मित वस्तुओं की कुल संख्या = 900

दुकान E द्वारा निर्मित मगों की संख्या = 900 * (11/18) = 550

दुकान E द्वारा निर्मित प्लेटों की संख्या = 900 - 550 = 350

उत्तर: C

दुकान A और D द्वारा निर्मित प्लेटों की औसत संख्या = (320 + 180)/2 = 250

दुकानों C और D द्वारा निर्मित मगों की औसत संख्या = (480 + 360)/2 = 420

आवश्यक प्रतिशत = [(420 - 250) * 100/420] = 40.47% कम

अतः, सही उत्तर विकल्प C है।

hindi.question: 144-लीटर मिश्रण A में दूध और पानी है, और दूध की मात्रा पानी की तुलना में 40% अधिक है। जब मिश्रण A का 2x लीटर निकाला जाता है, तो मिश्रण A में पानी की मात्रा (x + 5) लीटर हो जाती है। यदि मिश्रण B में 5x लीटर और (2x – 10) लीटर दूध और पानी है, तो मिश्रण B की कुल मात्रा ज्ञात करें।
hindi.explanation:
उत्तर: C

माना मिश्रण A में पानी की प्रारंभिक मात्रा 5b लीटर है।

तो, मिश्रण A में दूध की प्रारंभिक मात्रा = 1.4 * 5b = 7b लीटर

5b + 7b = 144

12b = 144

b = 12

मिश्रण A में पानी की प्रारंभिक मात्रा = 5 * 12 = 60 लीटर

मिश्रण A में दूध की प्रारंभिक मात्रा = 7 * 12 = 84 लीटर

60 – {2x * (5/12)} = x+ 5

x + (5x/6) = 60 - 5

(11x/6) = 55

x = 30

मिश्रण B में दूध की मात्रा = 5 * 30 = 150 लीटर

मिश्रण B में पानी की मात्रा = 2 * 30 – 10 = 50 लीटर

मिश्रण B में दूध और पानी की कुल मात्रा = (150 + 50) = 200 लीटर

अतः, सही विकल्प C है।

hindi.question: P, Q और R की वर्तमान आयु का योग 84 वर्ष है। छह वर्ष पहले, P की आयु R की आयु का तीन गुना थी, और उसी समय, Q, P से 4 वर्ष छोटा था। Q की वर्तमान आयु ज्ञात कीजिए।
hindi.explanation:
उत्तर: D

माना कि 6 वर्ष पहले R की आयु = x थी 

R की वर्तमान आयु = x + 6

6 वर्ष पहले P की आयु = 3x

P की वर्तमान आयु = 3x + 6

6 वर्ष पहले Q की आयु = 3x - 4

Q की वर्तमान आयु = 3x - 4 + 6 = 3x + 2

प्रश्न के अनुसार,

x + 6 + 3x + 6 + 3x + 2 = 84

7x + 14 = 84

7x = 70

x = 10

Q की वर्तमान आयु = 3x + 2 = 30 + 2 = 32 वर्ष 

अतः, सही उत्तर विकल्प D है।

hindi.question: एक संख्या और उसी संख्या के दोगुने का गुणनफल 392 है। संख्या ज्ञात कीजिए।
hindi.explanation:
उत्तर: C

प्रश्न के अनुसार,

x * 2x = 392

2x2 = 392

x2 = 196

संख्या = 14

hindi.question: एकसाथ पाइप A और B एक टैंक को 80 घंटे में भर सकते हैं, जबकि एकसाथ पाइप B और C एक टैंक को 60 घंटे में भर सकते हैं। एकसाथ पाइप A और B को 20 घंटे के लिए खोला जाता है, जिसके बाद पाइप A को बंद कर दिया जाता है। फिर एकसाथ पाइप B और C को 15 घंटे के लिए खोला जाता है, जिसके बाद पाइप B को बंद कर दिया जाता है। शेष टैंक अकेले पाइप C द्वारा 60 घंटे में भर जाता है। पूरे टैंक को भरने में अकेले पाइप C द्वारा लिया गया समय ज्ञात कीजिए।
hindi.explanation:
उत्तर: D

माना कुल कार्य = 240 इकाई (60 और 80 का लघुत्तम समापवर्त्य)

पाइप A और B की दक्षता = 240/80 = 3 इकाई

पाइप B और C की दक्षता = 240/60 = 4 इकाई

एकसाथ पाइप A और B को 20 घंटे भरने में लगा समय = 20 * 3 = 60 इकाई

एकसाथ पाइप B और C को 15 घंटे भरने में लगा समय = 15 * 4 = 60 इकाई

शेष 60 घंटों में अकेले C द्वारा टंकी भरने में लिया गया समय = 240 - 60 - 60 = 120 इकाई

C द्वारा अकेले एक घंटे में भरने में लिया गया समय = 120/60 = 2 इकाई

लिया गया समय = 240/2 = 120 घंटे

hindi.question: समकोण त्रिभुज का क्षेत्रफल 30 मी2 है और समकोण त्रिभुज का आधार उसकी ऊंचाई से x मीटर अधिक है और गोले का आयतन 38808 मी3 है। यदि समकोण त्रिभुज का आधार गोले की त्रिज्या से 9 मीटर कम है, तो समकोण त्रिभुज की ऊँचाई ज्ञात कीजिए।
hindi.explanation:
उत्तर: A

गोले का आयतन = 4/3(πr3)

4/3 * 22/7 * r3 = 38808

r3 = 9261

r = 21 मीटर

समकोण त्रिभुज का आधार = 21 – 9 = 12 मीटर

समकोण त्रिभुज की ऊँचाई = (12 – x) मीटर

समकोण त्रिभुज का क्षेत्रफल = 1/2 * b * h

1/2 * 12 * (12 - x) = 30

144 – 12x = 60

84 = 12x

x = 7 मीटर

समकोण त्रिभुज की ऊँचाई = 12 – 7 = 5 मीटर

hindi.question: एक बैग में 3 प्रकार की 90 रंगीन पेंसिलें हैं अर्थात सफेद, पीली और हरी हैं। पीली और हरी पेंसिलों की संख्या क्रमशः 'x' और 'y' है और सफेद पेंसिलों की संख्या 42 है। पीली पेंसिल निकालने की प्रायिकता बैग से हरी पेंसिल निकालने की प्रायिकता (4/15) अधिक है। बैग से हरी पेंसिल निकलने की प्रायिकता ज्ञात कीजिए।
hindi.explanation:
उत्तर: D

बैग से पीली पेंसिल निकालने की प्रायिकता = (x/90)

बैग से हरी पेंसिल निकालने की प्रायिकता = (y/90)

पीली पेंसिल निकालने की प्रायिकता = (4/15) + हरी पेंसिल निकालने की प्रायिकता

(x/90) = (4/15) + (y/90)

(x/90) – (y/90) = 4/15

(x-y)/90 = 4/15

x-y = 24 …समीकरण (1)

बैग में पेंसिलों की कुल संख्या = 90 और सफेद पेंसिलें = 42

तो, x + y + 42 = 90

x + y = 48 … समीकरण (2)

समीकरण (1) और (2) को बराबर करने पर हमें मिलता है, x= 36, y= 12

इसलिए, हरी पेंसिल निकालने की प्रायिकता = [(12C1)/ (90C1)] = 2/15

अतः, सही विकल्प D है।

hindi.question: यदि वस्तु O को उसकी लागत मूल्य से 20% अधिक अंकित किया है, तो उसी वस्तु पर दी गई छूट से होने वाली हानि का अनुपात ज्ञात कीजिए।
hindi.common_data:
निम्नलिखित जानकारी का ध्यानपूर्वक अध्ययन करें और नीचे दिए गए प्रश्नों के उत्तर दें।

एक दुकानदार ने तीन अलग-अलग वस्तुएँ - M, N, और O खरीदीं। वस्तुओं M और N की लागत मूल्यों का अनुपात क्रमशः 4: 5 है। वस्तु O का लागत मूल्य वस्तु M की तुलना में 200 रुपये अधिक है। वस्तु M को 20% के लाभ पर बेचा जाता है। वस्तु N को उसके लागत मूल्य से 40% अधिक अंकित किया जाता है और फिर अंकित मूल्य पर 10% की छूट पर बेचा जाता है। वस्तु N का विक्रय मूल्य 1,260 रुपये है। वस्तु O को 15% की हानि पर बेचा जाता है।
hindi.explanation:
माना वस्तु M का लागत मूल्य = 4a रुपये

english.explanation:
Answer: C

Given word: S W E E T

The third and fifth letter from the left end are E and T

Given Word: C A N D Y

The second and fourth letter from the left end are A and D

So, only one meaningful word can be formed, i.e., DATE.

So, the first letter from the left end of the meaningful word is D.

hindi.question:
कथन:

 A > B = C = D ≤ E; F ≥ G > H = I < A

निष्कर्ष:
hindi.common_data: दिए गए प्रश्नों में, विभिन्न तत्वों के बीच संबंध कथनों और उसके बाद दिए गए निष्कर्षों में दर्शाया गया है। वह निष्कर्ष ज्ञात कीजिए जो निश्चित रूप से सत्य है।
hindi.explanation:
उत्तर: B

a) D < I (D = C = B < A > I) ---> असत्य
b) F > I (F ≥ G > H = I) ---> सत्य
c) B > H (B < A > I = H) ---> असत्य
d) E < B (E ≥ D = C = B) ---> असत्य
e) G < A (G > H = I < A) ---> असत्य

कथन:

केवल कुछ बेंज(Benz) ऑडी(Audi) हैं।

केवल कुछ ऑडी(Audi) बीएमडब्ल्यू(BMW) हैं।

कोई फरारी(Ferrari) बीएमडब्ल्यू(BMW) नहीं है।

कुछ फरारी(Ferrari) कीवी(kiwi) हैं।

निष्कर्ष:

I. कुछ बेंज(Benz) बीएमडब्ल्यू(BMW) नहीं हैं।

hindi.question: अंतिम व्यवस्था के अनुसार पंक्ति में कितने व्यक्ति बैठे हैं?

  • पंक्ति में बैठे व्यक्तियों की संख्या 15 से अधिक है लेकिन 30 से अधिक नहीं है।

उपरोक्त शर्त से, केस 2 और केस 4 समाप्त हो जाती हैं, क्योंकि पंक्ति में बैठे व्यक्तियों की संख्या 15 से अधिक है लेकिन 30 से अधिक नहीं है, जो संतुष्ट नहीं है।

  • E, J और M के ठीक बीच में बैठा है।
  • E के बाईं ओर और दाईं ओर बैठे व्यक्तियों की संख्या एक अभाज्य संख्या है।

उपरोक्त शर्तों से, केस -1 समाप्त हो जाती है क्योंकि E के बाईं ओर और दाईं ओर बैठे व्यक्तियों की संख्या एक अभाज्य संख्या है, जो संतुष्ट नहीं है।

F, J से चार व्यक्ति वरिष्ठ है। जितने व्यक्ति A से वरिष्ठ हैं उतने ही व्यक्ति I से कनिष्ठ हैं। C, सीटीओ है। D, G से वरिष्ठ है लेकिन H से कनिष्ठ है, जो न तो सीईओ है और ना ही D से तत्काल वरिष्ठ है। J न तो टीम लीड और ना ही सहयोगी है। A, निदेशक से वरिष्ठ पदांकित है लेकिन सीओओ से कनिष्ठ है। E, B से तत्काल वरिष्ठ है, जो कनिष्ठतम पदांकित व्यक्ति नहीं है।
hindi.explanation:
अंतिम व्यवस्था:

हमारे पास है,

  • A, निदेशक से वरिष्ठ पदांकित है लेकिन सीओओ से कनिष्ठ है।

  • C, सीटीओ है।

उपरोक्त शर्तों से, दो संभावनाएं हैं।

फिर से, हमारे पास है

  • F, J से चार व्यक्ति वरिष्ठ है।

फिर से, हमारे पास है,

  • D, G से वरिष्ठ है लेकिन H से कनिष्ठ है, जो न तो सीईओ है और ना ही D से तत्काल वरिष्ठ है।

उपरोक्त शर्तों से, केस-1 और केस 1a समाप्त हो जाते हैं क्योंकि D, G से वरिष्ठ है लेकिन H से कनिष्ठ है, जो न तो सीईओ है और ना ही D से तत्काल वरिष्ठ है, जो संतुष्ट नहीं है।

अतः, केस-2a अंतिम व्यवस्था को दर्शाता है।

उत्तर: C

P, S के दाईं ओर चौथे स्थान पर बैठा है, जहाँ दोनों में से कोई भी एक अंतिम छोर पर बैठा है। जितने व्यक्ति P के दाईं ओर बैठे हैं उतने ही व्यक्ति U के दाईं ओर बैठे हैं। U, V के दाईं ओर चौथे स्थान पर बैठा है, जो किसी अंतिम छोर पर नहीं बैठा है। W, Y के बाईं ओर दूसरे स्थान पर बैठा है, जो न तो V के आसन्न बैठा है और ना ही S के समान दिशा में मुख करता है। T, W के आसन्न बैठा है। T और Q के बीच बैठे व्यक्तियों की संख्या एक पूर्ण वर्ग है लेकिन 1 से अधिक है। R, Q के तत्काल दाईं ओर बैठा है और दक्षिण की ओर मुख करता है।

अंतिम व्यवस्था:

हमारे पास है,

  • P, S के दाईं ओर चौथे स्थान पर बैठा है, जहाँ दोनों में से कोई भी एक अंतिम छोर पर बैठा है।
  • जितने व्यक्ति P के दाईं ओर बैठे हैं उतने ही व्यक्ति U के दाईं ओर बैठे हैं।

उपरोक्त शर्तों से, चार संभावनाएं हैं:

फिर से, हमारे पास है

  • U, V के दाईं ओर चौथे स्थान पर बैठा है, जो किसी अंतिम छोर पर नहीं बैठा है।

 उपरोक्त शर्त से, केस 3 और केस 4 समाप्त हो जाती हैं क्योंकि U, V के दाईं ओर चौथे स्थान पर बैठा है, जो किसी अंतिम छोर पर नहीं बैठा है, जो संतुष्ट नहीं है।

फिर से, हमारे पास है:

  • W, Y के बाईं ओर दूसरे स्थान पर बैठा है, जो न तो V के आसन्न बैठा है और ना ही S के समान दिशा में मुख करता है।
  • T, W के आसन्न बैठा है।
  • T और Q के बीच बैठे व्यक्तियों की संख्या एक पूर्ण वर्ग है लेकिन 1 से अधिक है।
  • R, Q के तत्काल दाईं ओर बैठा है और दक्षिण की ओर मुख करता है।

उपरोक्त शर्तों से, केस-1 समाप्त हो जाती है क्योंकि R, Q के तत्काल दाईं ओर बैठा है और दक्षिण की ओर मुख करता है, जो संतुष्ट नहीं है।

इसलिए, केस -2 अंतिम व्यवस्था को दर्शाती है।
